note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Actual archived Bob Harms whole flowering-specimen panel 1 shows several attached leafy shoots and panicles; panel 2 displays the entire dense short-branched seedhead; panel 3 magnifies overlapping glumes. A contracted ovoid to cylindrical head is a first clue (FNA 0.5–8 cm long, often 0.8–2 cm wide), but several introduced Phalaris look similar. The one- vs two-STERILE-LEMMA difference cannot be determined from head silhouette alone.
tiles.short: A compact, firm, green canarygrass head—not a fluffy awned foxtail
tiles.status: COMPLETE ATTACHED HEAD VISIBLE; SPECIES-LEVEL DISSECTION STILL NECESSARY

tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE ROOTED ANNUAL
tiles.details: This is a spring/cool-season annual, not a rhizomatous reed canarygrass colony. The archived mounted whole flowering specimen (panel 1) includes several basal culms, but roots are outside the visible image. Williamson County's detailed flora specifies fibrous-rooted, 1–several stems at base, NOT rosetted. Do not confuse the familiar pale compressed goosegrass crown with maygrass. Next field photo must show a properly identified attached stem, actual roots and the central crown with a centimeter scale.
tiles.short: Annual bunchgrass; exposed fibrous roots still missing
tiles.status: WHOLE FLOWERING HABIT PHOTOGRAPHED; ROOT SYSTEM NOT PHOTOGRAPHED

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE TWO GLUMES
tiles.details: Actual source photos (panels 3 and 4) show sharply keeled outer glumes. Flora of North America gives glumes about 3.8–6(8) mm, varying slightly with geography; the Williamson County detailed treatment gives roughly 4.8–5.3 mm with narrow keel wings. An image's generic black-white strip is NOT sufficient for a measured value until the original scale's physical units are documented. Isolate one ripe spikelet, photograph both glumes, and place a true millimeter ruler alongside.
tiles.short: A ~4–6 mm spikelet enclosed by two narrowly winged glumes
tiles.status: PUBLISHED DIMENSIONS; NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SEPARATED MEASURED GLUMES

tiles.heading: 04 · COUNT THE REDUCED STERILE FLORETS
tiles.details: Carolina canarygrass contains TWO distinguishable narrow sterile lemmas below a single fertile floret, commonly around 1.5–2.5 mm. Bob Harms's dissected spikelet composite (panel 4) shows opened floral structures but does NOT resolve and label each small sterile lemma unambiguously. Importantly, lesser canarygrass P. minor usually has ONE conspicuous sterile lemma plus another absent or VERY TINY vestige (~0.3 mm); some treatments count this vestige as a second sterile floret. So don't teach absolute 'two versus one total' without explaining the vestige. Match actual side-by-side dissected spikelets and measure both sterile lemmas separately. EXTRA ACTUAL GENUS-LEVEL PHOTO MODEL (panel 8): a separately photographed, source-authenticated P. arundinacea spikelet has the two thin reduced sterile lemmas visibly separated with a real 5-mm scale. THIS IS NOT P. CAROLINIANA and does not fill our species-specific dissection hold.
tiles.short: Two WELL-DEVELOPED reduced sterile lemmas; one fertile floret
tiles.status: REAL OTHER-SPECIES ANATOMY TEACHING MODEL ADDED; EXACT P. CAROLINIANA TWO-LEMMA DISSECTION STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · OPEN THE TRUE LEAF COLLAR
tiles.details: Bob Harms's true leaf junction plate (panel 5) already provides more than a vague head photo: pale blade/sheath lips and adjacent alternating dark/pale scale markings are visible. A true eciliate membrane is described for P. caroliniana (FNA usually 1.5–7 mm; Williamson County ~1–6.5 mm), not a hairs-only ligule. The free edge and original plate scale-unit calibration have not been demonstrated in this archived image. Do NOT arrow a sheath lip as the full ligule, or read precise mm from unverified bars. Photograph a peeled INNER junction with a labelled 1-mm rule.
tiles.short: Membranous ligule, not a tuft of hairs
tiles.status: ACTUAL COLLAR PHOTO WITH SCALE GRAPHIC; FREE EDGE/UNITS STILL UNVERIFIED

tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT LESSER CANARYGRASS
tiles.details: The current P. minor photo (panel 0) is a correctly distinguished OTHER-SPECIES whole head, not a matched floret dissection. P. caroliniana: two recognizable narrow reduced sterile lemmas typically 1.5–2.5 mm, glume keels narrowly winged. P. minor: usually one developed sterile lemma around 0.7–1.8 mm, with a second vestigial scale about 0.3 mm or absent; the glume wing often irregularly toothed. Crucial nuance: some botanical treatments count P. minor's minute scale and report TWO basal sterile florets; so compare DEVELOPMENT, not simply a hard yes/no floret tally. Introduced P. canariensis ALSO has two substantial sterile lemmas, but usually longer and broader glumes; native P. angusta can likewise have two but often shorter sterile structures. Use an opened mature spikelet, never head color or anther hue alone.
tiles.short: P. minor often has one obvious sterile lemma plus vestige
tiles.status: PRECISE OTHER-SPECIES COMPARISON; VERIFIED MM DISSECTION STILL PENDING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: CAROLINA CANARYGRASS (maygrass): look for a fairly firm, dense, oval-to-elongate light-green head with overlapping pointed, faintly green-and-pale-striped glumes, above flat shiny leaves on an ANNUAL grass. The true test is ONE dissected 4–6 mm spikelet: two narrow, hairy REDUCED STERILE florets below one fertile floret, surrounded by two keeled, narrowly winged glumes. Introduced lesser canarygrass (Phalaris minor) has ONE reduced sterile floret; head shape, flowering color and site moisture are insufficient by themselves. FIVE source-labelled physically archived Harms photos now show whole annual habit, entire flowering head, compact inflorescence details, individual spikelet, and photographed collar/sheath. They do NOT yet independently prove individual TWO inner sterile lemmas; count those in a dissected mature spikelet with true 1mm ruler. Original attribution copyrighted science/education, not CC.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: 1 · SEEDHEAD — View the Bob Harms whole head (teaching panel 2) and gross overlapping-glume macro (panel 3). Both are original source-identified species photos. The compact oblong-to-ovoid contracted panicle is an excellent field clue but not enough alone to separate P. minor.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Bob Harms's true leaf junction plate (panel 5) already provides more than a vague head photo: pale blade/sheath lips and adjacent alternating dark/pale scale markings are visible. A true eciliate membrane is described for P. caroliniana (FNA usually 1.5–7 mm; Williamson County ~1–6.5 mm), not a hairs-only ligule. The free edge and original plate scale-unit calibration have not been demonstrated in this archived image. Do NOT arrow a sheath lip as the full ligule, or read precise mm from unverified bars. Photograph a peeled INNER junction with a labelled 1-mm rule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Actual source photos (panels 3 and 4) show sharply keeled outer glumes. Flora of North America gives glumes about 3.8–6(8) mm, varying slightly with geography; the Williamson County detailed treatment gives roughly 4.8–5.3 mm with narrow keel wings. An image's generic black-white strip is NOT sufficient for a measured value until the original scale's physical units are documented. Isolate one ripe spikelet, photograph both glumes, and place a true millimeter ruler alongside.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: P. minor is the dangerous look-alike: similarly firm compact canarygrass head, usually one sterile floret (vs two in Carolina); P. minor's glume wings are often irregularly dentate, Carolina usually smoother/entire but variable. P. canariensis ALSO has two sterile florets: its glumes are markedly broader, typically 7–10 mm, with more obvious wings. P. angusta is generally more narrowly cylindrical and has shorter reduced sterile florets (~0.7–1.5 mm vs Carolina 1.5–2.5 mm). Polypogon monspeliensis has fine long awns giving a soft fuzzy head. P. arundinacea is perennial/rhizomatous with potentially spreading flowering branches; annual rooted base confirms against that species.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: REAL CULM NODE — actual stem joint above and below green internodes
panels.caption: An actual same-species, CC0 Texas close-up of a cylindrical stem, conspicuous banded joint and adjoining internodes. This is a true culm node, NOT an inner leaf ligule. No roots grow from this pictured joint.
panels.creator: iNaturalist photo contributor (recorded CC0)
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: INNER COLLAR PHOTO — real translucent membrane at blade–sheath junction
panels.caption: A Texas grass leaf deliberately held open so the blade, overlapping green sheath and pale translucent inner collar tissue can be inspected. The visible whitish flap is in the correct ligular region, but is not a fully spread or 1-mm-calibrated ligule measurement. Do not interpret the entire sheath margin as the ligule.
panels.creator: iNaturalist photo contributor (recorded CC0)
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

memory_rule: CAROLINA: TWO reduced sterile florets + one fertile inside paired keeled glumes. MINOR: ONE reduced sterile floret. The green dense head is a clue, NOT confirmation.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
